new_integration_decision: Use a lock-compatible cross-process archive admission test, not an unconditional both-process pre-append barrier. The current append_observations reads existing IDs and then appends without an interprocess critical section; a naive barrier inside that critical section would deadlock a correct serialized repair and create a false negative.

test_contract.fixture: Shared tmp_path observations.jsonl initially absent; spawn two independent processes with the identical valid FlowObservation payload/source_record_id and an explicit common start event; patch per-process storage.load_observations only to signal when pre-append read completes; do not require both processes to enter that read before releasing the first.
steps: Launch two spawn-context processes against the same archive, synchronize only process start; give process A a bounded post-read pause, release it whether or not process B reaches its own pre-read checkpoint (B may correctly wait behind a lock).
Join both processes with timeouts, propagate child exceptions and exit codes; require both to terminate cleanly.

Read the archive via load_observations and independently parse every nonempty JSONL line; assert exactly one row with the original observation_id and original provenance; assert append counts total exactly 1.
Repeat with two distinct IDs and assert exactly two parseable records with both IDs (no lost append); repeat a sequential identical replay and assert 0 new rows.
Keep two-writer output generation and reader-visible coherence as separate tests; identical as_of_ms is not a generation-identity oracle.
test_contract.note: A nondeterministic race stress test alone is insufficient proof; instrumented interleaving must be tested without blocking valid locking.
